sections.content: Use por *eso* to introduce a consequence. It connects one completed event with what happened as a result: *Recibió* una *noticia*, por eso se *fue*. The consequence normally follows por eso. Both parts can describe completed events with the pretérito indefinido.

items.spanish: Recibió una noticia, por eso se fue.
items.english: He received some news, so he left.

items.spanish: Terminó el viaje, por eso nos despedimos.
items.english: The trip ended, so we said goodbye.

items.spanish: Entendió la situación, por eso lloró.
items.english: She understood the situation, so she cried.

items.spanish: Quiso hablar, por eso se quedó.
items.english: He wanted to talk, so he stayed.

sections.content: Use porque to give the reason. Use por *eso* to introduce the consequence. Do not use por eso when you mean because.
